chapters.title: Nehemiah's Prayer
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 1

News from Jerusalem

1The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah.

And it came to pass in the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year, as I was in Susa the citadel,

2that Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah. I asked them about the Jews who had escaped, those who were left from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.

3They said to me, "The remnant there in the province who are left from the captivity are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."

4When I heard these words, I sat down and wept and mourned for days, and I was fasting and praying before the God of heaven.

The Prayer

5I said, "Please, LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and loyal love with those who love Him and keep His commandments,

6let Your ear be attentive and Your eyes open, to hear the prayer of Your servant that I am praying before You today, day and night, for the sons of Israel Your servants, confessing the sins of the sons of Israel, which we have sinned against You. Both I and my father's house have sinned.

7We have acted very corruptly against You and have not kept the commandments, the statutes and the rules that You commanded Moses Your servant.

8Remember the word that You commanded Moses Your servant, saying, 'If you break faith, I will scatter you among the peoples;

9but if you return to Me and keep My commandments and do them, even if your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place that I have chosen to make My name dwell there.'

10They are Your servants and Your people, whom You redeemed by Your great power and by Your strong hand.

11Please, Lord, let Your ear be attentive to the prayer of Your servant and to the prayer of Your servants who delight to fear Your name. Give success to Your servant today, and grant him mercy before this man."

I was cupbearer to the king.

Notes

  • v1 "The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah" — the book opens as a man's own account, and most of it is told in the first person.

  • v1 "in the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year" — the twentieth year of Artaxerxes (2:1), the ninth month of the year; the request to the king comes four months later, in Nisan.

  • v5 "the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and loyal love with those who love Him" — the words of Moses: the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loyal love with those who love Him and keep His commandments (Deuteronomy 7:9). Daniel's prayer opens with the same words (Daniel 9:4).

  • v6 "let Your ear be attentive and Your eyes open" — Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the house: let Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to the prayer made in this place (2 Chronicles 6:40). Both I and my father's house have sinned: he confesses with the people, not about them.

  • vv8–9 "If you break faith, I will scatter you… even if your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, I will gather them from there" — not one verse but the sense of several: I will scatter you among the nations (Leviticus 26:33), and if your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, from there the LORD your God will gather you (Deuteronomy 30:4). Break faith is ma'al, Ezra's word for the sin (Ezra 9:2).

  • v10 "by Your great power and by Your strong hand" — Moses' plea after the golden calf: whom You brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a strong hand (Exodus 32:11).

  • v11 "before this man… I was cupbearer to the king" — mashqeh, the office of Pharaoh's chief cupbearer in Joseph's story (Genesis 40:1–2). In the prayer, the king of Persia is this man.

chapters.title: Nehemiah Sent to Jerusalem
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 2

Before the King

1And it came to pass in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, when wine was before him, that I took up the wine and gave it to the king. I had not been sad in his presence before.

2The king said to me, "Why is your face sad, though you are not sick? This is nothing but sadness of heart." I was very much afraid.

3I said to the king, "May the king live forever! Why should my face not be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' graves, lies in ruins, and its gates have been consumed by fire?"

4The king said to me, "What are you asking for?" So I prayed to the God of heaven,

5and I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, send me to Judah, to the city of my fathers' graves, that I may rebuild it."

6The king said to me, with the queen sitting beside him, "How long will your journey be, and when will you return?" So it pleased the king to send me, and I set him a time.

7I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, let letters be given me to the governors of the province Beyond the River, so that they will let me pass through until I come to Judah,

8and a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel of the house, for the wall of the city and for the house that I will occupy." The king granted me this, for the good hand of my God was on me.

9I came to the governors of the province Beyond the River and gave them the king's letters. The king had sent with me officers of the army and horsemen.

10When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard this, it displeased them greatly that someone had come to seek the good of the sons of Israel.

The Walls Inspected by Night

11I came to Jerusalem and was there three days.

12Then I arose in the night, I and a few men with me. I told no one what my God had put into my heart to do for Jerusalem. There was no animal with me except the animal I was riding.

13I went out by night through the Valley Gate toward the Dragon's Spring and to the Dung Gate, and I examined the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and its gates, which had been consumed by fire.

14Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and to the King's Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to pass.

15So I went up by the valley in the night and examined the wall. Then I turned back and entered by the Valley Gate, and so returned.

16The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, for I had not yet told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials or the rest who were to do the work.

"Let Us Rise and Build"

17Then I said to them, "You see the trouble we are in, how Jerusalem lies in ruins and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let us build the wall of Jerusalem, so that we may no longer be a disgrace."

18I told them of the hand of my God, which had been good on me, and also of the words the king had spoken to me. They said, "Let us rise and build." So they strengthened their hands for the good work.

19But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite servant and Geshem the Arab heard of it, they mocked us and despised us and said, "What is this thing you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"

20I answered them, "The God of heaven, He will give us success, and we His servants will rise and build. But you have no portion, no right and no memorial in Jerusalem."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "I had not been sad in his presence… Why is your face sad, though you are not sick?" — maddua panekha ra'im, the question Joseph put to Pharaoh's cupbearer in prison: Why are your faces bad today? (Genesis 40:7). Now the cupbearer is the one with the sad face, and the king asks.

  • v3 "the city, the place of my fathers' graves" — he does not name Jerusalem. A letter to an Artaxerxes had called it that rebellious and wicked city, and the king had stopped its rebuilding (Ezra 4:12, 21); Nehemiah speaks of his fathers' graves.

  • v4 "So I prayed to the God of heaven, and I said to the king" — the prayer comes between the king's question and the answer, in the time it takes to draw breath.

  • v6 "with the queen sitting beside him" — ha-shegal, the word of the psalm, the queen stands at your right hand in gold of Ophir (Psalm 45:9).

  • v8 "the keeper of the king's forest" — pardes, a Persian word for an enclosed park, the word behind English paradise.

  • v8 "for the good hand of my God was on me" — Ezra's refrain (Ezra 7:6, 9, 28; 8:18, 22, 31), now in Nehemiah's mouth (also v18).

  • v10 "Tobiah the Ammonite servant" — the law says No Ammonite… shall enter the assembly of the LORD (Deuteronomy 23:3), and the book will end with Tobiah turned out of a chamber of the house (13:1–8).

  • v18 "So they strengthened their hands" — va-yechazzequ yedeihem, the reverse of the people of the land who kept weakening the hands of the people of Judah (Ezra 4:4).

  • v20 "no portion, no right and no memorial in Jerusalem" — cheleq u-tsedaqah ve-zikkaron: no share of the land, no legal claim, and no name remembered there.

chapters.title: The Builders of the Wall
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 3

From the Sheep Gate to the Valley Gate

1Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests, and they built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors. They consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel.

2Next to him the men of Jericho built, and next to them Zaccur son of Imri built.

3The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.

4Next to them Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired. Next to them Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, repaired. Next to them Zadok son of Baana repaired.

5Next to them the Tekoites repaired, but their nobles would not put their necks to the work of their lord.

6Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.

7Next to them Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon and of Mizpah, repaired, for the seat of the governor of the province Beyond the River.

8Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths, repaired. Next to him Hananiah, one of the perfumers, repaired, and they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.

9Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired.

10Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph repaired opposite his own house, and next to him Hattush son of Hashabneiah repaired.

11Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens.

12Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired, he and his daughters.

13Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate. They built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars, and repaired a thousand cubits of the wall, as far as the Dung Gate.

From the Dung Gate to the Water Gate

14Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate. He built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.

15Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He built it, roofed it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden, as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.

16After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, repaired as far as a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the pool that had been made, and as far as the house of the mighty men.

17After him the Levites repaired: Rehum son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, repaired for his district.

18After him their brothers repaired: Bavvai son of Henadad, ruler of half the district of Keilah.

19Next to him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section, opposite the ascent to the armory at the angle.

20After him Baruch son of Zaccai zealously repaired another section, from the angle to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.

21After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the door of the house of Eliashib to the end of the house of Eliashib.

22After him the priests, the men of the surrounding plain, repaired.

23After them Benjamin and Hasshub repaired opposite their own house. After them Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, repaired beside his own house.

24After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the angle and to the corner.

25Palal son of Uzai repaired opposite the angle and the tower that projects from the upper house of the king at the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh

26and the temple servants who lived on the Ophel repaired as far as a point opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.

From the Ophel Back to the Sheep Gate

27After them the Tekoites repaired another section, opposite the great projecting tower as far as the wall of the Ophel.

28Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each opposite his own house.

29After them Zadok son of Immer repaired opposite his own house. After him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, repaired.

30After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph repaired another section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his own chamber.

31After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the temple servants and of the merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper room of the corner.

32Between the upper room of the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and the merchants repaired.

Notes

  • vv1, 32 "the Sheep Gate" — the list begins and ends at the same gate and goes once around the city, gate by gate, section by section.

  • vv4–32 "repaired" — hecheziq, made strong, the verb of the chapter, said again and again of every family and every section. Next to him… after him carries the list around the wall as the work was done, side by side.

  • v1 "Eliashib the high priest… consecrated it" — the high priest's family takes the first gate, near the house, and consecrates it. His own house is on the wall (vv20–21).

  • v5 "their nobles would not put their necks to the work of their lord" — tsavvaram, their neck, as an ox's neck under a yoke. Adoneihem, their lords, may be Nehemiah and the officials, or the Lord. The Tekoites themselves did a second section (v27).

  • v8 "they restored Jerusalem" — va-ya'azvu, a verb that usually means leave, abandon. Here it can only mean something done to the wall; restored is the sense most widely given, and it is uncertain.

  • v12 "he and his daughters" — the only women named in the work on the wall.

  • v15 "the Pool of Shelah" — ha-Shelach, from shalach, to send, the conduit that sends the water; Isaiah's the waters of Shiloah that go gently (Isaiah 8:6) is written with the same letters.

  • v20 "zealously" — hecherah, from charah, the verb of anger that burns; here it is said of the work.

chapters.title: Building with a Weapon in Hand
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 4

The Mockery of Sanballat and Tobiah

1And it came to pass, when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, that he was angry and greatly enraged, and he mocked the Jews.

2He said before his brothers and the army of Samaria, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they bring the stones back to life out of the heaps of rubble, burned as they are?"

3Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him, and he said, "Even what they are building, if a fox went up on it, he would break down their stone wall!"

4Hear, our God, for we are despised. Turn their taunt back on their own heads, and give them up to be plundered in a land of captivity.

5Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You, for they have provoked You to anger before the builders.

6So we built the wall, and the whole wall was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.

The Plot and the Guard

7When Sanballat and Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of the walls of Jerusalem was going forward and that the breaches were beginning to be closed, they were very angry,

8and they all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and throw it into confusion.

9But we prayed to our God and set a guard against them day and night because of them.

10In Judah they said, "The strength of the burden bearers is failing, and there is too much rubble. We cannot build the wall."

11Our adversaries said, "They will not know or see until we come into their midst and kill them and stop the work."

12When the Jews who lived near them came, they said to us ten times, "From every place where you turn, they will come against us."

13So I stationed the people in the lowest parts of the space behind the wall, in the open places. I stationed the people by families, with their swords, their spears and their bows.

14I looked, and I rose and said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives and your homes."

15When our enemies heard that it was known to us, and God had frustrated their plan, we all returned to the wall, each to his work.

A Sword at Every Side

16And it came to pass from that day on that half of my servants did the work, while the other half held the spears, the shields, the bows and the armor, and the officers stood behind the whole house of Judah,

17who were building the wall. Those who carried burdens were loaded in such a way that each did the work with one hand and held his weapon with the other.

18Each of the builders had his sword strapped at his side as he built, and the man who sounded the horn was beside me.

19I said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "The work is great and spread out, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.

20Wherever you hear the sound of the horn, gather to us there. Our God will fight for us."

21So we did the work, while half of them held the spears, from the break of dawn until the stars came out.

22At that time I also said to the people, "Let every man and his servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may be a guard for us by night and work by day."

23Neither I nor my brothers nor my servants nor the men of the guard who followed me took off our clothes; each kept his weapon at the water.

Notes

  • vv1–23 — the Hebrew numbers vv1–6 as 3:33–38 and vv7–23 as 4:1–17. The rendering follows the English numbering.

  • v2 "Will they bring the stones back to life" — ha-yechayyu, make live, the verb for raising the dead, used of burned stones in the rubble.

  • vv4–5 "Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You" — the words of Jeremiah's prayer against those who plotted his death: Do not atone for their iniquity, and do not blot out their sin from before You (Jeremiah 18:23).

  • v12 "From every place where you turn, they will come against us" — the Hebrew is hard: from all the places that you return to us. The Greek reads They are coming up against us from all the places. The neighbors' warning is clear; its exact words are not.

  • v14 "Remember the Lord, great and awesome" — the words of Nehemiah's first prayer, the great and awesome God (1:5), now a battle cry.

  • v17 "each did the work with one hand and held his weapon with the other" — shelach, a weapon, a thrown spear or dart; the Greek has bolida, a javelin.

  • v20 "Our God will fight for us" — the word of Moses at the sea: The LORD will fight for you (Exodus 14:14).

  • v23 "each kept his weapon at the water" — the Hebrew is four words, ish shilcho ha-mayim, each his weapon, the water, and its sense is uncertain: perhaps that even going for water a man took his weapon. The Greek leaves the words out.

And it came to pass, when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, that he was angry and greatly enraged, and he mocked the Jews.

He said before his brothers and the army of Samaria, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they bring the stones back to life out of the heaps of rubble, burned as they are?"
Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him, and he said, "Even what they are building, if a fox went up on it, he would break down their stone wall!"
Hear, our God, for we are despised. Turn their taunt back on their own heads, and give them up to be plundered in a land of captivity.
Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You, for they have provoked You to anger before the builders.
So we built the wall, and the whole wall was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.
The Plot and the Guard

When Sanballat and Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of the walls of Jerusalem was going forward and that the breaches were beginning to be closed, they were very angry,
and they all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and throw it into confusion.
But we prayed to our God and set a guard against them day and night because of them.
In Judah they said, "The strength of the burden bearers is failing, and there is too much rubble. We cannot build the wall."
Our adversaries said, "They will not know or see until we come into their midst and kill them and stop the work."
When the Jews who lived near them came, they said to us ten times, "From every place where you turn, they will come against us."
So I stationed the people in the lowest parts of the space behind the wall, in the open places. I stationed the people by families, with their swords, their spears and their bows.

I looked, and I rose and said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives and your homes."
When our enemies heard that it was known to us, and God had frustrated their plan, we all returned to the wall, each to his work.
A Sword at Every Side

And it came to pass from that day on that half of my servants did the work, while the other half held the spears, the shields, the bows and the armor, and the officers stood behind the whole house of Judah,
who were building the wall. Those who carried burdens were loaded in such a way that each did the work with one hand and held his weapon with the other.
Each of the builders had his sword strapped at his side as he built, and the man who sounded the horn was beside me.
I said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "The work is great and spread out, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.
Wherever you hear the sound of the horn, gather to us there. Our God will fight for us."
So we did the work, while half of them held the spears, from the break of dawn until the stars came out.
At that time I also said to the people, "Let every man and his servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may be a guard for us by night and work by day."
Neither I nor my brothers nor my servants nor the men of the guard who followed me took off our clothes; each kept his weapon at the water.

chapters.title: The Outcry of the Poor
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 5

The Outcry

1There was a great outcry of the people and their wives against their brothers the Jews.

2Some were saying, "With our sons and our daughters, we are many. Let us get grain, so that we may eat and live."

3Some were saying, "We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards and our houses to get grain in the famine."

4Some were saying, "We have borrowed money for the king's tax on our fields and our vineyards.

5Our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, and our children are like their children, yet we are forcing our sons and our daughters into slavery. Some of our daughters have already been forced into it, and it is not in our power to help it, for our fields and our vineyards belong to others."

Nehemiah Rebukes the Nobles

6I was very angry when I heard their outcry and these words.

7I took counsel with myself and brought charges against the nobles and the officials. I said to them, "You are exacting interest, each from his brother!" Then I held a great assembly against them.

8I said to them, "We, as far as we were able, have bought back our brothers the Jews who had been sold to the nations, but you are selling your own brothers, so that they may be sold to us!" They were silent and could find nothing to say.

9I said, "What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, because of the taunts of the nations, our enemies?

10I too, and my brothers and my servants, are lending them money and grain. Let us stop this interest.

11Give back to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves and their houses, and the hundredth part of the money, the grain, the new wine and the oil that you are exacting from them."

12They said, "We will give it back and require nothing from them. We will do as you say." I called the priests and made them swear to do as they had promised.

13I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, "So may God shake out every man from his house and from his labor who does not keep this promise. So may he be shaken out and emptied." All the assembly said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. The people did as they had promised.

Nehemiah's Example

14Moreover, from the day I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes the king, twelve years, neither I nor my brothers ate the governor's food allowance.

15The former governors who were before me laid heavy burdens on the people and took from them food and wine, besides forty shekels of silver. Even their servants lorded it over the people. But I did not do so, because of the fear of God.

16I also held fast to the work on this wall, and we bought no land, and all my servants were gathered there for the work.

17At my table were a hundred and fifty men, Jews and officials, besides those who came to us from the nations around us.

18What was prepared for one day was one ox and six choice sheep, and birds were prepared for me, and every ten days all kinds of wine in abundance. Yet for all this I did not ask for the governor's food allowance, because the service was heavy on this people.

19Remember me, my God, for good, for all that I have done for this people.

Notes

  • vv1, 6 "a great outcry… their outcry" — tsa'aqah, za'aqah, the cry the LORD heard from Israel in Egypt: I have heard their outcry because of their taskmasters (Exodus 3:7). Now the cry is against brothers.

  • v5 "Our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers" — ki-vsar acheinu besarenu. The words Judah used of Joseph when he proposed to sell him: he is our brother, our flesh (Genesis 37:27). The poor use them against brothers who are selling them.

  • v7 "You are exacting interest, each from his brother" — massa… nosh'im, from nasha, to lend at interest, the word of the law: you shall not be a creditor to him (Exodus 22:25); You shall not charge interest to your brother (Deuteronomy 23:19).

  • v8 "We… have bought back our brothers… but you are selling your own brothers" — the law of redemption: a brother sold to a guest living among you may be bought back by his kin (Leviticus 25:47–49), and a brother who sells himself to you must not be made to serve as a slave (25:39).

  • v13 "I also shook out the fold of my garment" — chotsni, the fold at the chest where things were carried. Emptied before them, it shows what will happen to any man who breaks the oath.

  • v14 "from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes" — the year Nehemiah came (2:1) to the year he went back to the king (13:6).

  • v19 "Remember me, my God, for good" — Nehemiah's short prayer, his own signature. It returns, in nearly the same words, at the end of the book (13:14, 22, 31).

chapters.title: The Wall Finished
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 6

The Plots against Nehemiah

1And it came to pass, when it was reported to Sanballat and Tobiah and to Geshem the Arab and to the rest of our enemies that I had built the wall and that no breach was left in it, though up to that time I had not set up the doors in the gates,

2that Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, "Come, let us meet together at Kephirim in the plain of Ono." But they were planning to do me harm.

3So I sent messengers to them, saying, "I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?"

4They sent to me four times in this way, and I answered them in the same way.

5The fifth time Sanballat sent his servant to me in the same way, with an open letter in his hand.

6In it was written: "It is reported among the nations, and Geshem says it too, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel; that is why you are building the wall. According to these reports, you are to become their king,

7and you have also set up prophets to proclaim about you in Jerusalem, 'There is a king in Judah.' Now this will be reported to the king according to these words. So now come, and let us take counsel together."

8I sent to him, saying, "No such things as you say have been done; you are inventing them out of your own heart."

9For they all wanted to frighten us, thinking, "Their hands will drop from the work, and it will not be done." But now, strengthen my hands.

The Hired Prophet

10I went into the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was shut in at home, and he said, "Let us meet at the house of God, inside the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple, for they are coming to kill you. By night they are coming to kill you."

11But I said, "Should a man like me run away? Would a man like me go into the temple and live? I will not go in."

12Then I understood that God had not sent him, but that he had spoken the prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.

13He was hired for this purpose, that I should be afraid and act in this way and sin, and so they would have a bad name to taunt me with.

14Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these deeds of theirs, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets who wanted to make me afraid.

The Wall Finished

15So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul, in fifty-two days.

16When all our enemies heard of it, all the nations around us were afraid and fell greatly in their own eyes, for they knew that this work had been done by our God.

17In those days also the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah's letters came to them.

18For many in Judah were bound to him by oath, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.

19They also kept speaking of his good deeds in my presence and reporting my words to him, and Tobiah sent letters to make me afraid.

Notes

  • v3 "I sent messengers to them, saying, 'I am doing a great work'" — mal'akhim, messengers, and melakhah, work, from the same root, la'akh, to send on an errand. They send for him; his errand is the wall.

  • v5 "an open letter" — not sealed, so that the servant and anyone along the way could read it. The charge of rebellion is spread as it is delivered.

  • v7 "There is a king in Judah" — the charge Ezra's enemies brought: a city rebellious and harmful to kings (Ezra 4:15).

  • vv10–11 "inside the temple… would a man like me go into the temple and live?" — ha-heikhal, the house itself, where only the priests may enter. The law says the outsider who comes near shall be put to death (Numbers 18:7), and King Uzziah was struck with blight for going in (2 Chronicles 26:16–21). Nehemiah is not a priest; to hide there would itself be the sin (v13).

  • v14 "Noadiah the prophetess" — ha-nevi'ah, the title of Miriam, Deborah and Huldah. Here it is given to a prophetess who works against him.

  • v15 "the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul, in fifty-two days" — Elul is the sixth month. The wall that had lain broken since Babylon burned it was closed in less than two months.

  • v16 "fell greatly in their own eyes" — va-yippelu me'od be-eineihem: their confidence fell, as the wall rose.

  • v18 "the son-in-law of Shecaniah… the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah" — Meshullam built two sections of the wall (3:4, 30). Tobiah the Ammonite is married into the families doing the work.
